subject: Simulating and analysing an AR1 time series with negative binomial distribution

messages.author: a22e8a7b2a35fc51
messages.subject: Simulating and analysing an AR1 time series with negative binomial distribution
parts:
Hi,

I'm trying to analyse some simulated data, but can't get decent estimates of the input parameters I provided to the simulation.

I am generating a bunch of time series, each with it's own mean/intercept, and with negative binomial observations.

I have taken bits of code from examples in the nbinomial.pdf and ar1.pdf documents and hacked them together thus:

library(INLA)
#
n_series <-  50 # num time series, each with own mean
l_series <- 100 # length of time series
# AR1 parameters
rho  <- 0.8
prec <- 10
# Neg binomial size
sz <- 150
# simulate data
series_av <- rnorm(n_series, mean=5, sd=1)
DF <- do.call( rbind, lapply( 1:n_series, function(s){
 eta <- as.vector( arima.sim( list( order=c(1,0,0), ar=rho ), n=l_series,
                              sd=sqrt(1/prec) ) )
 eta <- eta+series_av[s]
 obs <- rnbinom( l_series, mu=exp(eta), size=sz )
 return(data.frame(obs,yr=1:l_series,s=rep(s,l_series),eta))
} ) )
#
result <- inla( obs ~ factor(s)-1+f(yr,model="ar1",replicate=s),
                family="nbinomial", data=DF )

One run of this gives me:

                                                           mean          sd
size for the nbinomial observations (overdispersion) 91.4917581 16.18338374
Precision for yr                                      3.6360234  0.17871476
Rho for yr                                            0.8128775  0.01020611

So the estimated size and precision vary considerably from my simulation inputs (150 and 10).

I don't know whether my error is in my simulation, analysis model or basic understanding? Probably some combination of the three.

Any comments appreciated.

Regards,
Ron.

I don't think this is really a problem, but you simulated the factor using a Gaussian, which would mean:
result <- inla( obs ~ f(s, model="iid")+f(yr,model="ar1",replicate=s), ...)

Here, you recover sigma_s = 1 and intercept = 5.

On Mon, 2017-02-27 at 05:07 -0800, rcdr...@gmail.com wrote:
>


the issue seems to be that argument 'sd' in arima.sim, is _not_ the
marginal stdev, but the stdev of the innovation process, and the
marginal variance is var.innovation/(1-phi^2). you can check this
adding 'scale' which will scale to unit scale (and subtract the mean,
but that is a minor issue), and then scale it


 eta <- as.vector( sqrt(1/prec) * scale(arima.sim( list(
order=c(1,0,0), ar=rho ), n=l_series)))


which seems to give the correct results.

H
--
Håvard Rue
he...@r-inla.org
